llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed wrapper for a third-party image-generation CLI, but users should notice that it can send prompts and selected local files to dLazy and may spend API credits.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, commands, API endpoints, authentication, prompt submission, local image upload behavior, and hosted output URLs all fit an image-generation SaaS integration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include generic image-generation terms, which could route broad image requests to this paid external service; the hard error-handling wording is also stronger than necessary but is limited to auth and balance guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The install path uses npm/npx for @dlazy/cli@latest, while the prose inaccurately describes the install spec as pinned to 1.0.9; this is a supply-chain clarity issue, not evidence of malicious behavior in the skill artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network calls to api.dlazy.com and files.dlazy.com, prompt transfer, and user-specified media uploads are disclosed and proportionate for cloud image generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The CLI stores a dLazy API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json or accepts DLAZY_API_KEY; this credential persistence is clearly disclosed and revocable, with no background worker or unrelated persistence shown.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you are comfortable using dLazy as the image provider, sending prompts and selected media files to its service, storing or passing a dLazy API key, and using an npm package installed or run with @latest rather than a pinned version.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad English and Chinese trigger phrases are a real routing concern because they may invoke this external paid SaaS for generic image requests, but the underlying image-generation behavior and data flows are disclosed and purpose-aligned.
[SQP-3] expected: Guiding the agent to explain insufficient balance or missing API-key errors is expected for this integration; the imperative wording should be treated as documentation guidance rather than host-policy override.
